scenes.heading: Quadrilaterals
scenes.say: Doors, phone screens, tiles and kites. They all have four sides. Is a square a rectangle? By the end of this video, you'll know for sure.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A family where children inherit their parents' traits
scenes.science: A square has every property of a rectangle AND a rhombus
scenes.breaks: in a family a child isn't also the parent, but a square really is a rectangle, a rhombus and a parallelogram.
scenes.say: Think of quadrilaterals as a family. They all share four sides, the family name. Some members inherit extra features. A square has everything a rectangle has, and everything a rhombus has. Unlike a real family, a square really is a rectangle and a rhombus at the same time.

scenes.heading: Angle sum
scenes.say: Draw one diagonal and any quadrilateral splits into two triangles. Two lots of one hundred and eighty is three hundred and sixty. So the four angles always add to three hundred and sixty degrees.
scenes.caption: Draw one diagonal and any quadrilateral splits into two triangles. 2 × 180° = 360°. So the four angles always add to 360°.

scenes.heading: The special ones
points: Square: a rectangle AND a rhombus
Trapezium: exactly 1 pair of parallel sides
scenes.say: A parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides. Give it right angles and it's a rectangle. Give it four equal sides and it's a rhombus. Do both and it's a square. A trapezium has exactly one pair of parallel sides. And a kite has two pairs of equal sides next to each other.

scenes.heading: Parallelogram angles
scenes.question: One angle of a parallelogram is 65°. Find the other three.
scenes.say: One angle of a parallelogram is sixty-five degrees. The opposite angle is equal, so it's sixty-five too. Neighbouring angles add to one eighty, so the next one is one hundred and fifteen, and so is the one opposite it. They add to three sixty. Perfect.
scenes.caption: One angle of a parallelogram is 65°. The opposite angle is also 65°. Neighbouring angles add to 180°, so the others are 115° each. Total: 360°.

scenes.heading: Finding a missing angle
scenes.question: A quadrilateral has angles 100°, 80°, 95° and d°. Find d.
scenes.say: A quadrilateral has angles one hundred, eighty, ninety-five and d. The known ones add to two hundred and seventy-five. Three sixty minus two seventy-five is eighty-five. So d is eighty-five.
scenes.caption: Angles 100°, 80°, 95° and d°. The known ones add to 275. 360 − 275 = 85. So d = 85.

points: Trapezium: exactly 1 pair of parallel sides
scenes.say: Quick recap. Quadrilateral angles add to three sixty. A square is a rectangle and a rhombus. Parallelograms have equal opposite angles. A trapezium has one pair of parallel sides. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Quick recap. Quadrilateral angles add to 360°. A square is a rectangle and a rhombus. Parallelograms have equal opposite angles. A trapezium has one pair of parallel sides. Now try the practice questions!
